Based on my search, I can provide you with a comprehensive overview of the bones of the head (skull).

## Overview

The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). These bones are primarily connected by immovable fibrous joints called **sutures**. The skull is divided into two main parts:

1. **Neurocranium (Cranium)** - the braincase that protects the brain
2. **Viscerocranium (Facial Skeleton)** - the bones that form the face

---

## Cranial Bones (8 bones)

The cranium forms the protective housing for the brain and is composed of:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** (1) | Forms the forehead and superior portion of the eye sockets; contains frontal sinuses |
| **Parietal bones** (2) | Form the sides and roof of the cranial vault |
| **Temporal bones** (2) | Form the sides and base of the cranium; house structures of the middle and inner ear |
| **Occipital bone** (1) | Forms the back and base of the skull; contains the **foramen magnum** (where spinal cord connects to brain) |
| **Sphenoid bone** (1) | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base of the skull; contains the sella turcica (houses pituitary gland) |
| **Ethmoid bone** (1) | Located between the orbits; forms part of the nasal cavity and contains the cribriform plate |

---

## Facial Bones (14 bones)

The facial skeleton comprises:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** (1) | The lower jaw; the **only movable bone** of the skull |
| **Maxillae** (2) | Upper jaw; form part of the orbit and most of the hard palate |
| **Zygomatic bones** (2) | Cheekbones; form part of the lateral walls of the orbits |
| **Nasal bones** (2) | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones** (2) | Small bones in the medial walls of the orbits; house the lacrimal sac |
| **Palatine bones** (2) | Form the posterior part of the hard palate |
| **Inferior nasal conchae** (2) | Project into the nasal cavity; aid in airflow regulation |
| **Vomer** (1) | Forms the inferior portion of the nasal septum |

---

## Key Sutures (Joints Between Bones)

- **Coronal suture** - between frontal and parietal bones
- **Sagittal suture** - between the two parietal bones
- **Lambdoid suture** - between parietal and occipital bones
- **Squamous suture** - between parietal and temporal bones

---

## Additional Associated Bones

- **Hyoid bone** - located in the neck; not part of the skull proper, but associated with it; provides attachment for tongue and larynx muscles
- **Auditory ossicles** (6 total: 3 in each ear) - malleus, incus, and stapes in the middle ear

---

## Main Functions of Skull Bones

1. **Protection** - of the brain, eyes, and other sensory organs
2. **Support** - for facial structures and muscles
3. **Housing** - for special sense organs (sight, smell, taste, hearing, balance)
4. **Openings** - numerous foramina allow passage of cranial nerves and blood vessels

Sources:
1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull
2. https://www.osmosis.org/learn/Bones_of_the_cranium
3. https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/osteology/skull/
4. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
5. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
6. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
7. https://anatomy.co.uk/skull
